catalog.name: Water Quality & Ocean Color
catalog.description: Satellite-derived water quality and ocean color products from MODIS and VIIRS missions providing essential information for aquatic ecosystem health assessment and water resource management.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Ocean color products from NASA MODIS and VIIRS missions, processed by NASA Ocean Biology Processing Group (OBPG). Chlorophyll algorithms developed by NASA Ocean Color team. Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Ocean color products support water quality monitoring and aquatic ecosystem research applications.

info.name: Water Quality Applications
info.content: These products enable monitoring of eutrophication, harmful algal blooms, water clarity, and overall aquatic ecosystem health in both marine and freshwater environments.

info.name: Freshwater Monitoring
info.content: While optimized for ocean applications, these products also provide valuable information for large lakes, reservoirs, and coastal waters affecting freshwater resources.

members.name: Chlorophyll Concentration
members.description: Chlorophyll-a concentration products indicating phytoplankton biomass and primary productivity in aquatic systems.

members.name: MODIS Chlorophyll-a (Terra, Daily)
members.description: Daily chlorophyll-a concentration from MODIS Terra satellite indicating phytoplankton biomass and water quality conditions.

info.name: Background
info.content: Chlorophyll-a is the primary photosynthetic pigment in phytoplankton and serves as a proxy for phytoplankton biomass and primary productivity in aquatic ecosystems.

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Chlorophyll-a concentration in milligrams per cubic meter (mg/m³)

info.name: Algorithm Basis
info.content: Uses ocean color algorithms based on blue-green light ratios that correlate with chlorophyll concentration in the water column

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 4 km spatial resolution optimized for regional to global scale aquatic ecosystem monitoring

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: February 2000 to present, daily global coverage from Terra satellite

info.name: Water Quality Indicator
info.content: High chlorophyll levels may indicate eutrophication, nutrient pollution, or harmful algal blooms; low levels may indicate oligotrophic (nutrient-poor) conditions

info.name: Applications
info.content: Eutrophication monitoring, harmful algal bloom detection, aquatic ecosystem health assessment, water quality management, fisheries productivity evaluation

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, NASA Ocean Biology Processing Group (OBPG)

members.name: MODIS Chlorophyll-a (Aqua, Daily)
members.description: Daily chlorophyll-a concentration from MODIS Aqua satellite providing complementary observations for enhanced aquatic ecosystem monitoring.

info.name: Background
info.content: MODIS Aqua provides complementary chlorophyll-a observations to Terra MODIS, with different overpass times enabling better temporal coverage and cloud gap reduction.

info.name: Overpass Time
info.content: Aqua satellite has afternoon overpass (~1:30 PM local time) complementing Terra's morning overpass (~10:30 AM local time)

info.name: Enhanced Coverage
info.content: Combined Terra and Aqua observations provide improved daily aquatic ecosystem monitoring with reduced cloud gaps

info.name: Applications
info.content: Enhanced water quality monitoring when combined with Terra, improved harmful algal bloom detection, comprehensive aquatic ecosystem assessment

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, NASA Ocean Biology Processing Group (OBPG)

members.name: VIIRS Chlorophyll-a (Daily)
members.description: Daily chlorophyll-a concentration from VIIRS with enhanced spatial resolution for detailed water quality assessment.

info.name: Background
info.content: VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) provides enhanced chlorophyll-a measurements with higher spatial resolution than MODIS for more detailed aquatic ecosystem monitoring.

info.name: Enhanced Resolution
info.content: 750m spatial resolution providing significantly higher detail than MODIS 4km chlorophyll products

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: January 2012 to present from Suomi NPP satellite, with continuing operations planned

info.name: Detailed Monitoring
info.content: Higher resolution enables monitoring of smaller water bodies, coastal areas, and detailed spatial patterns of phytoplankton distribution

info.name: Applications
info.content: High-resolution water quality mapping, detailed harmful algal bloom monitoring, coastal water quality assessment, small lake ecosystem studies

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA/NOAA VIIRS mission team, NASA Ocean Biology Processing Group (OBPG)

members.name: Water Turbidity & Clarity
members.description: Water turbidity and clarity indicators derived from satellite observations for assessing sediment loads and water quality conditions.

members.name: MODIS Water Vapor (Terra, Daily)
members.description: Daily water vapor measurements providing atmospheric moisture content information for weather and climate studies.

info.name: Background
info.content: Water turbidity measurements indicate the amount of suspended particles in water, providing information about sediment loads, erosion impacts, and overall water clarity.

info.name: Measurement Principle
info.content: Uses visible light reflectance patterns to estimate suspended sediment concentrations and water clarity

info.name: Turbidity Impacts
info.content: High turbidity reduces water quality, affects aquatic habitat, reduces photosynthesis in aquatic plants, and impacts drinking water treatment costs

info.name: Sediment Sources
info.content: Turbidity can indicate soil erosion, urban runoff, construction activities, dredging operations, and natural sediment transport processes

info.name: Applications
info.content: Water quality assessment, erosion monitoring, construction impact evaluation, drinking water source protection, aquatic habitat assessment

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, water quality algorithm development teams

members.name: MODIS Water Vapor (Aqua, Daily)
members.description: Daily water vapor measurements from MODIS Aqua satellite providing atmospheric moisture content for meteorological applications.

info.name: Background
info.content: Suspended sediment concentration provides quantitative measures of particulate matter in water bodies, essential for understanding water quality and sediment transport processes.

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Suspended sediment concentration typically expressed in milligrams per liter (mg/L)

info.name: Environmental Significance
info.content: Suspended sediments transport nutrients and pollutants, affect light penetration, and influence aquatic ecosystem health and productivity

info.name: Monitoring Applications
info.content: Tracking construction impacts, monitoring dam removal effects, assessing watershed management effectiveness, evaluating dredging operations

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, sediment algorithm development teams

members.name: Colored Dissolved Organic Matter
members.description: Colored Dissolved Organic Matter (CDOM) products indicating organic carbon content and water quality characteristics.

members.name: MODIS Cloud Water Path (Terra)
members.description: Daily cloud water path measurements indicating liquid water content in clouds for atmospheric and climate studies.

info.name: Background
info.content: CDOM consists of dissolved organic compounds that absorb light, particularly in blue wavelengths. It serves as an indicator of dissolved organic carbon and water quality conditions.

info.name: Organic Carbon Indicator
info.content: CDOM levels correlate with dissolved organic carbon concentrations, providing insights into terrestrial organic matter inputs and water quality

info.name: Sources and Impacts
info.content: CDOM originates from terrestrial vegetation, soil organic matter, and aquatic biological processes. High levels can affect water treatment and aquatic ecosystem light conditions

info.name: Water Quality Relevance
info.content: CDOM affects water color, light penetration, and photochemical processes, influencing aquatic ecosystem dynamics and water treatment requirements

info.name: Applications
info.content: Water quality monitoring, dissolved organic carbon assessment, terrestrial-aquatic carbon cycling studies, water treatment planning

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, ocean color algorithm development teams

members.name: Advanced Ocean Color Products
members.description: High-resolution and advanced ocean color products from MODIS and VIIRS missions providing enhanced capabilities for detailed marine ecosystem monitoring and water quality assessment.

members.name: MODIS Aqua High-Resolution Chlorophyll-a (L2)
members.description: High-resolution Level 2 chlorophyll-a concentration from MODIS Aqua satellite providing detailed ocean productivity measurements at full spatial resolution for coastal and marine ecosystem studies.

info.name: Background
info.content: Level 2 (L2) chlorophyll-a products provide the highest spatial resolution ocean color data available from MODIS Aqua, maintaining the native 1km resolution for detailed coastal and marine ecosystem monitoring.

info.name: Enhanced Resolution
info.content: Native 1km spatial resolution (versus 4km for Level 3 products) enables detailed monitoring of coastal waters, upwelling zones, and small-scale ocean features

info.name: Swath Coverage
info.content: Provides coverage along satellite swaths rather than gridded products, offering maximum spatial detail for specific regions and dates

info.name: Coastal Applications
info.content: Excellent for coastal water quality monitoring, estuarine studies, coral reef ecosystem assessment, and near-shore marine productivity analysis

info.name: Marine Ecosystem Detail
info.content: Captures fine-scale features like frontal boundaries, eddy structures, river plume dynamics, and upwelling patterns critical for marine ecosystem understanding

info.name: Research Applications
info.content: Ideal for detailed oceanographic research, validation studies, algorithm development, and high-resolution marine ecosystem modeling

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: July 2002 to present from MODIS Aqua satellite with continuing operations

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS Aqua mission, NASA Ocean Biology Processing Group (OBPG), Level 2 algorithm development team

members.name: VIIRS High-Resolution Chlorophyll-a (L2)
members.description: Ultra-high resolution Level 2 chlorophyll-a concentration from VIIRS providing the most detailed satellite-based ocean productivity measurements available for comprehensive marine ecosystem assessment.

info.name: Background
info.content: VIIRS Level 2 chlorophyll-a represents the current state-of-the-art in satellite ocean color observations, providing unprecedented spatial resolution for marine ecosystem monitoring and coastal water quality assessment.

info.name: Ultra-High Resolution
info.content: Native 750m spatial resolution, the highest available for operational satellite ocean color products, enabling detailed coastal and inland water monitoring

info.name: Advanced Sensor Technology
info.content: VIIRS incorporates improved sensor design and calibration compared to MODIS, providing enhanced data quality and more accurate retrievals

info.name: Small Water Body Monitoring
info.content: Resolution sufficient for monitoring large lakes, reservoirs, coastal lagoons, and other water bodies previously difficult to assess with satellite data

info.name: Coastal Zone Excellence
info.content: Superior performance in coastal waters where traditional ocean color algorithms face challenges due to complex optical properties

info.name: Continuity and Innovation
info.content: Continues the MODIS ocean color record while providing technological advances in sensor design and data processing capabilities

info.name: Climate Data Record
info.content: Part of NOAA's Climate Data Record program ensuring long-term continuity for climate and ecosystem monitoring applications

info.name: Applications
info.content: Detailed coastal water quality assessment, small lake monitoring, coral reef ecosystem studies, harmful algal bloom detection, marine protected area monitoring

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA/NOAA VIIRS Suomi NPP mission, NASA Ocean Biology Processing Group (OBPG), NOAA Climate Data Record program

members.name: Ocean Optical Properties
members.description: Advanced ocean optical property measurements providing detailed information about marine atmosphere interactions, aerosol properties over oceans, and water column optical characteristics.

members.name: Ocean Angstrom Exponent
members.description: Ocean Angstrom Exponent from MODIS Aqua providing information about aerosol particle size distribution over oceanic regions, critical for ocean-atmosphere interaction studies and marine air quality assessment.

info.name: Background
info.content: The Angstrom Exponent describes the wavelength dependence of aerosol optical depth, providing information about aerosol particle size distribution. Over oceans, it helps characterize marine aerosols and their interactions with ocean processes.

info.name: Particle Size Information
info.content: Higher Angstrom Exponent values (>1.5) indicate smaller particles like sea salt and pollution aerosols; lower values (<1.0) suggest larger particles like sea spray and dust

info.name: Ocean-Atmosphere Coupling
info.content: Provides insights into ocean-atmosphere interactions including sea spray generation, marine boundary layer processes, and transport of continental aerosols over oceans

info.name: Marine Air Quality
info.content: Important for understanding air quality over oceanic regions, shipping lane impacts, and the role of oceans in global aerosol and climate systems

info.name: Spatial Coverage
info.content: Focuses on oceanic regions where specialized algorithms optimize aerosol retrievals over water surfaces with low reflectance

info.name: Climate Applications
info.content: Essential for climate model validation, ocean-atmosphere interaction studies, marine aerosol characterization, and understanding oceanic contributions to global aerosol systems

info.name: Research Applications
info.content: Oceanographic research, marine meteorology, sea spray aerosol studies, shipping emission impacts, island and coastal aerosol transport

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS Aqua mission, aerosol retrieval algorithms optimized for ocean surfaces

members.name: VIIRS Ocean-Land Aerosol Optical Thickness
members.description: Advanced aerosol optical thickness over both land and ocean from VIIRS NOAA-20 satellite providing comprehensive atmospheric clarity assessment for air quality and climate applications with enhanced coastal coverage.

info.name: Background
info.content: VIIRS Dark Target Aerosol Optical Thickness provides state-of-the-art aerosol measurements over both land and ocean surfaces using advanced algorithms that leverage VIIRS improved sensor capabilities.

info.name: Unified Land-Ocean Retrievals
info.content: Advanced algorithm provides seamless aerosol optical thickness measurements across land-ocean boundaries, critical for coastal air quality and atmospheric transport studies

info.name: Enhanced Coastal Coverage
info.content: Improved retrieval capabilities in coastal zones where land-ocean transitions create challenging conditions for traditional satellite aerosol algorithms

info.name: VIIRS Sensor Advantages
info.content: Benefits from VIIRS improved calibration, enhanced spectral channels, and better spatial resolution compared to heritage MODIS sensors

info.name: Air Quality Applications
info.content: Comprehensive air quality monitoring across terrestrial and marine environments, coastal pollution assessment, atmospheric transport studies

info.name: Climate Monitoring
info.content: Part of operational climate monitoring systems providing consistent aerosol observations for climate model validation and trend analysis

info.name: Operational Continuity
info.content: Continues and enhances the MODIS aerosol climate data record while providing technological improvements for next-generation atmospheric monitoring

info.name: Research Applications
info.content: Advanced atmospheric research, air quality model validation, climate impact studies, coastal environmental monitoring

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA/NOAA VIIRS NOAA-20 mission, Dark Target aerosol algorithm development team, operational climate monitoring program
